Priyom — attaching redlines from Acme legal and procurement. Two points we need clarity on before we can proceed to our internal approval: 

1) Limitation of liability (Section 9) currently caps liability at fees paid in the prior 12 months and disclaims consequential damages. Our counsel is pushing back: they want an explicit carve-out so that termination for convenience entitles us to a refund of prepaid fees. They say a broad LoL that excludes consequential damages could be read to deny refunds or wind-down damages.

2) Wind-down assistance: we need a clear commitment and a way to quantify it. If Redwood requires notice and charges for wind-down, Acme needs to know how that will be offset against any refund.

Please confirm whether Redwood is willing to: (a) accept an explicit carve-out that refunds unused prepaid fees on termination for convenience, and (b) define wind-down assistance as either a time-limited support obligation (e.g., 30 days of support) or a capped credit so offsets are predictable.

Priyom / team — reviewed Acme's redlines and their counsel notes. Below are two discrete options we can present. I kept the language short so it can be inserted as a clean edit to Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) and Section 6 (Term & Termination).

Legal-preferred (limits exposure, defensible):
- Retain existing LoL cap (aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months).
- Add carve-out for (i) willful misconduct and (ii) breaches of confidentiality or data protection obligations (these remain uncapped).
- Explicitly state: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, amounts payable by Redwood to Customer on account of (a) refunds of prepaid, unused fees resulting from a Customer's termination for convenience, and (b) amounts reasonably necessary to effectuate the transition of services (wind-down assistance) shall be calculated in accordance with the Order Form and, solely to the extent set forth therein, are recoverable by Customer."
- Add a definition of "wind-down assistance" in the Order Form to mean a finite set of activities (knowledge transfer, runbook handoff, up to 30 days of technical support) and state that Redwood's liability for cash refund will be reduced by any credits or in-kind services provided under that assistance.

Sales-preferred (commercially generous, clearer):
- LoL cap remains the aggregate fees paid in the prior 12 months except for the carve-outs noted above.
- Termination for convenience: Customer entitled to a pro-rata refund of any prepaid, unused fees for the remainder of the current billing period, calculated on a daily basis, less: (i) any unpaid fees; and (ii) a wind-down assistance fee equal to up to 10% of the unused prepaid balance (or an equivalent 30 days of technical assistance).
- Provide an explicit Order Form schedule (Termination Schedule) that shows refund formula and dollar examples.

Recommend offering the sales-preferred language as a first commercial concession but with (1) a hard cap that refunds in aggregate cannot exceed fees paid in prior 12 months, and (2) the 10% wind-down offset to avoid open-ended exposure. If Acme pushes for cash refunds without offset we push back and escalate.

I've attached a redlined snippet you can send to Acme (Redwood_proposed_MSA_edits_20261014.docx).

Quick commercial view — Acme is strategic and fast to expand if onboarding goes well. I prefer the sales-preferred with the 10% wind-down offset (or equivalent 30 days in-kind) because:
- It gives Acme a visible win on refunds (which procurement cares about) but preserves our economic exposure.
- Example: 12-month prepay of $240k (monthly $20k). If they terminate at month 4, unused prepaid = $160k. Refund = $160k - 10% wind-down ($16k) = $144k cash (or $160k minus 30 days of support).

If legal insists on any additional carve-out language, we should still keep a global cap (fees paid in prior 12 months) so the worst-case remains bounded.

Authorize me to offer the sales-preferred language with a one-time concession that the wind-down offset can be cash OR service credit depending on Acme preference. I will not offer anything that increases the overall cap.

Anna — thanks for the redlines and for flagging the concern. We discussed internally and propose the following compromise language and commercial approach to keep momentum while protecting both parties.

Proposed contract language (clean, to be inserted into Section 9 and the Order Form Termination Schedule):

"Notwithstanding Section 9 (Limitation of Liability), the following amounts are recoverable by Customer: (a) refunds of any prepaid, unused fees resulting from a Customer's termination for convenience; and (b) amounts reasonably necessary to effectuate the transition of services ('Wind-Down Assistance'), each subject to the calculation rules in the applicable Order Form. Refunds of prepaid, unused fees shall be calculated on a pro-rata, daily basis for the remainder of the prepaid period. Refunds shall be net of any unpaid fees and a Wind-Down Offset equal to the lesser of (i) ten percent (10%) of the unused prepaid balance, or (ii) the value of up to thirty (30) days of Wind-Down Assistance as specified in the Order Form. For the avoidance of doubt, the aggregate liability of Redwood (including any refunds or Wind-Down Offsets) shall not exceed the sum of fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months prior to the event giving rise to liability, except for liabilities arising from willful misconduct or breaches of confidentiality/data protection obligations, which shall remain uncapped."

Commercially: we can accept a pro-rata refund less the 10% offset (or equivalent 30 days of assistance) and will include a Termination Schedule on the Order Form with worked examples. The refund mechanism will be cash by default; Customer may elect service credit in lieu of cash if mutually agreed.

Next steps: if that language is acceptable in principle we will prepare a tracked-change MSA and a Termination Schedule (with numeric examples) for signature. Attached: Redwood_proposed_MSA_edits_20261014.docx and a draft OrderForm_TerminationSchedule.xlsx showing the formula.

If Acme prefers a different offset formula (e.g., fixed fee or specific dollar cap), we can consider but will need to update the overall liability cap accordingly. If we need to escalate for executive sign-off I will notify you.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this piece quickly.
